gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each 'works without Wi-Fi' claim actually covers. Epson's CO-W01 is HDMI-only with nothing built in. Aurzen's ZIP mirrors a phone with no router but can't show Netflix, Hulu or Disney+. Google TV's offline 'basic TV' mode cannot install apps or cast. Nebula's own steps for playing from a USB drive on the Capsule 3 Laser start with installing two Google Play apps, which needs internet at least once.
standout_why: I compared against innovativeprojector.com (a seller blog) and nexttools.net, plus the rival pages I could open. innovativeprojector.com says only that some smart models need 'online activation' and that Wi-Fi Direct mirroring 'varies'. It names no models and gives no rule for any OS. nexttools.net says mirroring without Wi-Fi 'is not possible', which Aurzen's own ZIP help center contradicts. It never mentions Google TV. ChatGPT's answer says USB drives work 'provided the projector supports video playback'. It does not say that on Android/Google TV projectors this can depend on Play Store apps, or that Google's offline mode blocks installing them. I could not read the rival Aurzen ZIP Pro page (aurzen.com returned HTTP 429 three times), so I can't rule out that it states some of the mirroring point.
decides: It decides the pick for the shopper's 'nothing — projector should play movies by itself' and 'phone' options. (1) A Google/Android TV projector (Nebula Capsule 3, XGIMI MoGo 4, Aurzen BOOM mini) is a safe 'no Wi-Fi' choice only if the shopper can get it online once. Once set up as basic TV it cannot install apps or cast. Nebula's USB playback steps for the Capsule 3 Laser need two Play Store apps. (2) For a phone with no network at all, the Aurzen ZIP/ZIP Pro type with router-free mirroring fits. Streaming-app DRM content still won't mirror, so downloaded or local files only. The ZIP Pro also takes laptop video over a USB-C (DisplayPort Alt Mode) cable. (3) For a laptop or console, ChatGPT's Epson CO-W01 card is right. It is HDMI-only with no built-in streaming apps, so it never asks for Wi-Fi. Its 3,000 lumens is ISO 21118 white and IDMS 15.4 colour, a different scale from the unlabelled '200 lumens' a reviewer gave for the ZIP Pro.

findings.label: What Google TV's 'basic TV' mode allows without internet or a Google account
findings.value: Allowed: play from other inputs plugged into the device; use a limited set of pre-installed apps. Not allowed: install apps, cast from another device, use services that need a Google sign-in. It can only be chosen during setup. Once full Google TV is set up you need a factory reset to switch.
findings.source_title: Google TV Help: Use basic TV
findings.note: Google's wording: basic TV is 'only for TVs with Google TV built in'. I found no maker statement that the Nebula Capsule 3 GTV, XGIMI MoGo 4 or Aurzen BOOM mini offers it. Nebula's setup is reported to include a Wi-Fi and Google-account step, but I couldn't read the manual text (the PDF's text was unreadable to my fetch tool).

findings.label: Steps to play video from a USB drive without Wi-Fi (Nebula support)
findings.value: 1) Download videos to a USB drive. 2) Install the File Explorer app from the Google Play Store. 3) Install a media player app. 4) Connect the drive and play. Drive limits: up to 4 TB, FAT32 or NTFS only.
findings.source_title: How do I play videos without Wi-Fi? (Nebula/soundcore support)
findings.note: The article names only the Capsule 3 Laser (Android TV). Steps 2 and 3 use the Play Store, which needs an internet connection at least once. That is the footnote behind the 'USB playback' tick for this Android TV model. I could not find an equivalent article for the Capsule 3 Google TV model.

findings.label: Mirroring with no router
findings.value: Supported: 'The Aurzen ZIP supports Wi-Fi-free screen mirroring' (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows).
findings.note: The page's FAQs cover the original ZIP, not the ZIP Pro. It notes an over-the-air update and the AurzenHub app for an iPhone 17 mirroring issue.

findings.label: Wired input and DRM limit
findings.value: No built-in HDMI port; one USB-C port for charging (PD). Content from Netflix, Hulu, Disney+ and similar 'cannot be mirrored or wirelessly cast'.
findings.note: Aurzen's suggested workaround is its separate CastPlay wireless HDMI dongle. The help center does not mention USB flash-drive playback.

findings.label: Wired video input
findings.value: Two USB-C ports: one for charging and S/PDIF audio, one for video input (DisplayPort Alt Mode). No HDMI mentioned.
findings.source_title: Gizmochina, Aurzen ZIP Pro full review (Soumyakanti, 2026-10-31)
findings.note: Named reviewer. The review lists AirLink, Miracast, AirPlay P2P, DLNA and Google Cast for wireless. It says 'You cannot directly cast content from streaming platforms like Netflix and Hulu'; the workaround is a laptop over USB-C DP Alt Mode.

findings.label: Brightness, resolution, battery and price (reviewer)
findings.value: 200 lumens (no standard stated); native 1080p DLP; about 2.5 h measured by the reviewer in Normal mode (Aurzen claims up to 2.5 h in Eco); listed at $629.99, discounted to $579.99
findings.source_title: Gizmochina, Aurzen ZIP Pro full review (Soumyakanti, 2026-10-31)
findings.note: The price is as the reviewer reported it on 2026-10-31, not today's maker-store price. aurzen.com and storecheck both returned HTTP 429, so I could not confirm today's price.

findings.label: Brightness and how it is rated
findings.value: 3,000 lm colour brightness (IDMS 15.4) and 3,000 lm white brightness (ISO 21118)
findings.note: The only candidate here whose brightness is stated with a test standard. The ZIP Pro's 200 lumens has no standard stated, so the two can't be directly compared.

findings.label: How content gets to it
findings.value: One built-in HDMI port; no built-in streaming apps (you plug in an external streaming stick)
findings.note: It has no smart OS, so there is no Wi-Fi setup step. The product page does not list USB ports or a media player.
